led.purpose: Every count, tally, sum, and beat label — Doto dot-matrix with tabular figures.

display.purpose: Headings, names, tags, chips — Barlow Condensed uppercase.

body.purpose: Ribbon narration and verdict standfirst — Barlow 14px, stepping to 15px at ≥640px; story, disclosures, and roster labels hold 14px; capped 75ch.

label.purpose: The smallest marks — Barlow Condensed uppercase: verdict headline/side/disclosure labels and the majority-line caption at 11px (0.14em); the primary action runs the register large at 14px.

scale.purpose: Every size step the app renders — 11·12·13·14·15·16·18·24·30·48·60·72·96px — enumerated in DESIGN.md frontmatter typography.scale; per-step roles below.

steps.tag: 12px — chips, token-row tags, statuses, out-captions, section headings (Condensed 600); personas, captions, subtitle at phone width (Barlow 400); the playback beat chip (Doto 700).
steps.name: 13px — lane full names (Condensed 500, 0.08em); glossary tooltip definitions at ≥640px (Barlow 400).
steps.copy: 14px — narration base: ribbon and standfirst at phone width, story, disclosures, roster labels (Barlow 400); lane short tags and the primary action (Condensed 600); token counts, story tags, transfer pins (Doto 700).
steps.copy-wide: 15px — the narration step at ≥640px: ribbon text and verdict standfirst (Barlow 400).
steps.count: 16px — the majority line's threshold numeral (Doto 700); the roster steppers' glyphs (Condensed 700).
steps.chip: 18px — the ribbon's round chip, weight inputs, 100-sum readout (Doto 700); verdict-side names (Condensed 600, 0.04em).
steps.marquee: 24px — the h1 page name at phone width (Doto 900).
steps.verdict: 48px — the verdict card's counts at phone width (Doto 900).
steps.tally: 60px — lane tallies at phone width and verdict counts at ≥640px (Doto 900).

narrative.overview:
The election is a live game on one board. A near-black arena ground carries four team lanes with huge lamp-lit tallies, a physical majority line drawn at 51, a ribbon caption strip that narrates every change, and the 100 ballots massed courtside as physical tokens. There is no explainer chrome, no Sankey diagram, no setup wizard: the board is edited by hand (one board, two grips), the count is performed on it, and the strike — one bold diagonal — kills an eliminated lane. Every number on the page is a scoreboard digit; every sentence the board speaks runs through the ribbon.

The system is dark because the subject is a scoreboard at night, not because dark mode was chosen by category. Every surface is a step of a single cool near-black ramp (ground 950 → 400); text inks are tinted from the ground hue and never gray. The four candidate inks are Okabe-Ito-derived and pairwise distinct under deuteranopia and protanopia; a candidate is the same ink everywhere. Buzzer amber is a reserved channel: the majority line, the buzzer mark, and exactly two elements on a changed verdict.
keyCharacteristics: One near-black ground ramp; no surface outside it; text tinted from its hue
One ink per candidate, colorblind-safe, everywhere that candidate appears
LED dot-matrix numerals (Doto) for every count; signage grotesque (Barlow / Barlow Condensed) for every word
Buzzer amber reserved for threshold moments; ink everywhere else
The ribbon narrates; the strike decides; the tokens mass in chunks of five

rules.name: The Buzzer Reservation Rule
rules.body: Amber appears only where a threshold is crossed: the majority line, the buzzer mark, and the changed verdict’s two marks. If amber shows up anywhere else, the reveal is broken.

rules.name: The One Ink Per Candidate Rule
rules.body: Each candidate has exactly one ink keyed to their id, used in every surface they touch. Never recolor a candidate by state, mood, or chart position.

rules.name: The Never Gray Rule
rules.body: Text inks are tinted from the ground hue, never neutral gray; disabled means sunken onto a deeper bed, not faded toward gray.

rules.name: The Smallest Poster Rule
rules.body: The board's poster at share scale is the favicon — an authored in-world SVG (hand-drawn for this world; no raster asset ships anywhere): the four cast inks in lane order as a 2×2 quad of square 6px cells on ground-950, 1px gutters, no amber — the reservation holds even off the page. The link card (meta description, og:title, og:description, og:type website) and the browser chrome (theme-color = ground-950) dress from the same tokens.

rules.name: The Numbers Are LED Rule
rules.body: Every count, tally, sum, and beat label renders in the Doto register with tabular figures; prose never shows a bare number where a tally can carry it.

rules.name: The 75ch Ribbon Rule
rules.body: Narration and disclosure copy cap at 75ch; captions at 38ch. A score bug states, it does not paragraph.

rules.name: The Flat Floor Rule
rules.body: Floor panels cast no shadows; a surface’s height is its ground step. Only objects that physically float above the floor drop one: the strike and the glossary tooltip. If a card needs a shadow to separate, its ground step is wrong.

rules.name: The Square Court Rule
rules.body: Structure is square; only finger-scale controls may round (tokens 3px, chips pill). A rounded panel is from another world.

dos: Do render every count in the Doto LED register with tabular figures.
Do set a candidate’s color only through their cast ink, by id, in every surface.
Do mirror every board state change in the ribbon text — one announcer, one announcement per change.
Do keep amber for thresholds only; spend it on at most two elements at the verdict.
Do chunk vote tokens in groups of five; each mass states its own number.
Do let the persona read in full at every lane width — it wraps (three lines at phone width, two at ≥1024px) and is never clamped.
Do theme the browser’s own surfaces: ink-bright selection and caret, the 2px offset focus ring, dark color-scheme, theme-color on ground-950, and the four-ink favicon at share scale.
Do honor reduced motion two ways: the OS query and the in-app toggle both zero every animation and transition app-wide.
donts: Don’t introduce a neutral gray, a shadowed panel, or a rounded card — depth is a ground step, corners are square.
Don’t brighten a struck lane; the dim IS the meaning (“out”), with the caption and persona carrying the legible channel.
Don’t add a second live region, a kicker/eyebrow label, gradient text, or glyph icons.
Don’t let the 100-sum drift: the editor conserved electorate (placed + pool = 100) is visual law — show the sum, gate the primary on it.
Don’t load a fourth type family or pull fonts from a CDN; the three registers are self-hosted.
